page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server is configured with 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. Memory capacity reaches 256.0 GB, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for advanced vector and matrix math extensions such as AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8, along with cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI. The instance contains no integrated local storage and does not include GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show balanced compute output across single- and multi-core operations. The processor registers a strong single-core Geekbench score of 1942.0 and a multi-core score of 15353.0, paired with a multi-core stress-ng metric of 27932.88. Throughput in single-threaded tasks is complemented by solid results in text and image processing benchmarks, as well as high static web serving throughput of 54.65 GB/sec. On CPU-based LLM inference, small model text generation reaches top-tier speeds of 390.88 tokens per second, assisted by Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, though memory-specific benchmark suites like PassMark record weaker standalone memory scores.

The 256.0 GB RAM footprint offers high memory density for in-memory systems, supporting Redis workloads at 43.89 million SET operations per second and steady database transaction throughput. Lacking local storage, all operational data persistence requires external network-attached volumes, representing an operational tradeoff for I/O-intensive services. Microsoft Azure E32s_v6 fits memory-heavy deployments such as large-scale in-memory caches, relational and transactional database management systems, enterprise resource planning, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E32s_v6 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores at 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high 8:1 memory-to-core allocation. The CPU architecture includes AMX and AVX-512 instruction extensions for accelerated matrix math and encryption workloads. The server includes no local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and has zero bundled GPUs. Benchmark metrics demonstrate strong Geekbench single-core execution (1942.0), high static web serving throughput (54.65 GB/sec), and top-tier small model LLM text generation rates (390.88 tokens/sec). In-memory caching performance remains stable with 43.89 million Redis SET operations per second. The E32s_v6 is suitable for relational database engines, in-memory caches, enterprise applications, and memory-intensive analytics.
